newsitem.title: USA: Homestake, Santa Fe deal has $65 mln backout fee.
newsitem.headline: Homestake, Santa Fe deal has $65 mln backout fee.

text.p: Homestake Mining Co and Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp said Monday that if one of them backed out of their $2.3 billion friendly stock merger, $65 million would have to be paid to the jilted party.

In a conference call detailing the agreement, the companies also said they would shut Santa Fe's Albuquerque, N.M., headquarters as part of the expected elimination of overlap that will save $30 million in the deal's first year.
Santa Fe Chairman Patrick James said the companies had been talking about a transaction since March and Homestake made a formal bid in early November.
The Santa Fe-Homestake pact left Newmont Mining Co without a deal, its less-lucrative, unsolicited bid for Santa Fe passed over in favor of Homestake's bid.
James said that days before Newmont unveiled its stock-swap merger proposal last Thursday, Santa Fe rejected the bid and proceeded with its merger with Homestake.
Homestake said it expects to take $50 million in one-time charges related to the Santa Fe deal. It said the merger will be accretive to earning after the charges.

Jack Thompson, Homestake president and chief executive officer, who will become chairman and CEO of the merged companies, said he expects the combined companies to have $260 million in capital expenditures next year.
